title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 266
paragraphs: These observances, then, and others besides which I shall mention, the Hellenes have adopted from the Egyptians; but in making the images of Hermes with the phallos, as they do, they have learnt not from the Egyptians but from the Pelasgians. The custom was received first by the Athenians of all the Hellenes, and from them by the rest. For just at the time when the Athenians were beginning to be counted among the Hellenes, the Pelasgians became dwellers with them in their land, and from this very circumstance they began to be counted as Hellenes. Whoever has been initiated in the mysteries of the Cabeiri, which the Samothracians perform (having received them from the Pelasgians), that man knows the meaning of my speech. For those very Pelasgians who became dwellers with the Athenians used to dwell before that time in Samothrace, and from them the Samothracians received their mysteries. So then the Athenians were the first of the Hellenes to make the images of Hermes with the phallos, having learnt the practice from the Pelasgians; and the Pelasgians told a sacred story about it, which is set forth in the mysteries in Samothrace.
